name: NeuroSurge
model_scope: Separate model under development; no trained decoder is supplied or validated by this game.
signal_origin: simulated, unitless brain and muscle activity values
source_lineage: Body update (R558), third upload, built from the 10 November interaction update: a camera at your eyes with a 90-degree view; a long-sitting body with every limb forward and a slight bend in a stretched elbow or knee; the mirror body as a literal reflection on the same ground; 54 motor areas, one colour each, shared by the brain area and its muscles on both bodies, with a neon flash and one line from a lit area to the body part it moves; movements held until the opposite area or Reset body; Space as the one hand key (hold or tap to take hold of the brain, the mirror body or a limb, tap twice to turn all four limbs); reach keys that light only the shoulder and elbow parts of the strip and their muscles; an information card that names the strip part, the movement and the muscles, read with the R key; the glass brain in the upper part of the view with the mirror body below it, and a motor strip about 42 % of the view wide at 1920 by 1080; a numbered list of each motor area’s movements on the information card, done with the number keys 1 to 9, with “already there” on a movement that would not move the body; the left and right arrow keys stepping the look one motor area along the strip; an information card that takes an area when the look rests on it; a “Looking at” line that names the area and then its movement, and a card line that names the strip part and the half of the brain; a “Try this” guide that starts with area, number key, another body part and watching the body; knees that bend all the way and a hip area that swings the thigh down and back as well as up, out and in; a shorter Esc page with sentences that say what the motor strip is; stop-at-contact between the three items; a closed skull, eyes and 111 more muscles from BodyParts3D and Z-Anatomy; a cel-shaded comic look with gloss, lighter ink outlines, inked folds on the motor strip and an HDR glow; symmetric placement of paired controls; two performance passes. DESIGN-DECISIONS.md sections 20-66 record each change and why. The input-robustness changes published on 11 November (input epochs, deferred input, pointer capture) are included, adapted to the new keys, with their test files.
anatomy_assets: 611 human-anatomy OBJ files. BodyParts3D 4.0 (CC BY 4.0), including the new packets bodyparts3d-head-r1 (cranium and eyes) and missing-muscles-r1 (93 files); Z-Anatomy derivatives (CC BY-SA 4.0): the face muscles and 18 back, belly, neck and foot muscles in missing-muscles-r1. Packet files are unchanged archive members or documented conversions; runtime transforms, lifting, smoothing of finger and toe tips, colouring, comic shading and separated layers are display changes, not physiological validation.
code_licence: Project-owned contributions: CC0-1.0. Third-party material retains its own licences and notices.
known_engineering_gaps: Frame rate in the author's scripted runs at 1920 by 1080 on one desktop computer (three runs): 60 fps sitting still, 59-60 looking around, 52-59 in the slow limb turn, 50-53 while holding or carrying the mirror body, 52-58 in the view over the shoulder. Some frames still take longer than a thirtieth of a second (up to 50 ms while carrying the mirror body into contact). The layout changed since the second upload, so these numbers are not a like-for-like comparison with it. More performance work is still to do.

Ease of use and teaching: this upload's changes (brain above the body, numbered movements, arrow-key steps, the guide's new order, the teaching sentences) were checked by the author with scripted input only. No learner or teacher has tried them, and nothing here shows that the game teaches motor neuroanatomy better than before.

The motor strip is about 42 % of the view wide at 1920 by 1080; the user asked for 50 %. The brain's bottom arrow sits below the brain's frame edge rather than on it, so that it does not cover the mirror body.

Controls asked for and not built yet: the look swinging a held item round you with the same face toward you; the mirror body's top and bottom arrows orbiting instead of sliding it away and back; part-way joint positions by brain activation (a movement goes to its end stop); lowering the left arm from the strip (the left shoulder area lists no movements; the arm follows the look and the W A S D keys).
The left shoulder can come away from its socket at a far-left look, and the left shoulder muscle can show a pointed edge. Neither is fixed.
Limbs pass through each other: one limb does not knock another about.
Some motor areas cannot be aimed at until the brain is turned to one side. The count of such areas has not been redone for the 54-area map.
A one-way look lock after a far side look while an item rests against you was reported in the first upload and has not been checked again.

The 11 November input-robustness work (pointer capture boundaries, stale-input cancellation, deferred input queue) is included and covered by scripted tests; it has not been tried in several browsers.
Joint mechanics, whole-body coupling, motor-area registration and timing remain simplified and unvalidated. The body order along the strip is a simplified textbook order.
launcher_scope: Online URL launchers for Windows, macOS and Linux. Formats checked; native Windows/macOS use unverified. Prior Linux installation/launch does not prove execution of this updated target.
publication_status: Experimental preview. Since 12 November 2026 each finished version is uploaded at the user's direct instruction, before the project's independent review. Check the displayed online version before assuming it matches these files.

browser_verification.scope: Author development checks only: scripted mouse and key input in one desktop Chromium, with screenshots, frame-interval counts and profiles, plus seventeen scripted node tests (eleven files) of the input rules, the picture-quality controller, the number keys, the guide order, the card's settle rule, the arrow-key steps and the words that name an area. Earlier parts were also read and checked by other instances of the same model that wrote them; the changes since the second upload were checked by their author alone. No independent review yet. Not checked: Firefox, Safari, touch, phones, screen readers, reduced-motion settings in a browser.
